gaps.lead: The plane had just taken off when the warning light appeared.
gaps.sentence: The plane had ___ when the warning light appeared.
gaps.explanation: had just + participle = a very short time before.

gaps.lead: Only after reading the letter twice did it make sense.
gaps.sentence: The letter ___ sense until it had been read twice.
gaps.explanation: It made sense only after two readings = it didn't make sense until it had been read twice.

gaps.lead: 'I'm sorry I was rude to your sister,' Maria said.
gaps.sentence: Maria apologised ___ rude to my sister.
gaps.explanation: apologise for + -ing (or having + participle for the earlier action).

gaps.sentence: They announced that ___ selling the house.
gaps.explanation: we → they; present continuous → past continuous: they were selling.

gaps.lead: He'd rather not discuss the matter.
gaps.explanation: would prefer + not + to-infinitive: prefer not to discuss.

gaps.lead: The flat was too small for their growing family.
gaps.sentence: The flat wasn't ___ for their growing family.
